questions.stem: $18\ \mathrm{g}$ of a non-volatile solute is dissolved in $200\ \mathrm{g}$ of $\mathrm{H_2O}$ freezes at $272.07\ \mathrm{K}$. Calaculate the molecular mass of solute ($K_f$ for water $= 1.86\ \mathrm{K\,kg\,mol^{-1}}$)
questions.solution:
Given: $K_f = 1.86$; $w_A = 200\ \mathrm{g}$; $w_B = 18\ \mathrm{g}$; $M_B = ?$ (½)
$\Delta T_f = T_f^{o} - T_f = 273.15 - 272.07 = 1.08$
$\Delta T_f = K_f m = K_f \times \frac{w_B}{M_B} \times \frac{1000}{w_A}$
$1.08 = 1.86 \times \frac{18}{M_B} \times \frac{1000}{200}$ (1)
$M_B = 155\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$ (½)

questions.stem:
Calculate emf of the following cell at $25^\circ\mathrm{C}$ :
$\mathrm{Sn/Sn^{2+}\ (0.001\ M)\ ||\ H^{+}\ (0.01\ M)\ |\ H_{2}(g)\ (1\ bar)\ |\ Pt(s)}$
Given : $E^\circ(\mathrm{Sn^{2+}/Sn}) = -0.14\ \mathrm{V}$, $E^\circ \mathrm{H^+/H_2} = 0.00\ \mathrm{V}$ ($\log 10 = 1$)
questions.solution:
$E_{cell} = E^{o}_{cell} - \frac{0.0591}{2}\log\frac{[\mathrm{Sn^{2+}}]}{[\mathrm{H^+}]^{2}}$ (½)
$E^{o}_{cell} = 0 - (-0.14\ \mathrm{V}) = 0.14\ \mathrm{V}$ (½)
$E_{cell} = 0.14 - \frac{0.0591}{2}\log\frac{[0.001]}{[0.01]^{2}}$ (1)
$= 0.14 - \frac{0.0591}{2}\log 10$
$= 0.11\ \mathrm{V}$ (1)
(Deduct ½ marks for incorrect or no unit)

questions.stem: What that the time required for 99.9% completion in a first order reaction is 10 times of half-life ($t_{1/2}$) of the reaction [$\log 2 = 0.3010$, $\log 10 = 1$]
questions.solution:
$k = \frac{0.693}{t_{1/2}}$
$k = \frac{0.693}{10}$ (1)
$t = \frac{2.303 \times 10}{0.693}\log\frac{100}{100-99.9}$
$t = \frac{23.03}{0.693}\log 3$ (1)
$t = 99.69 \approx 100\ \mathrm{min}$ (½ + ½)
(or by any other suitable method)

questions.stem:
The nature of bonding, structure of the coordination compound can be explained to some extent by valence bond theory. The central metal atom/ion makes available a number of vacant orbitals equal to its coordination number. the appropriate atomic orbitals (s, p and d) of the metal hybridise to give a set of equivalent orbitals of definite geometry such as square planar, tetrahedral, octahedral and so on. A strong covalent bond is formed only when the orbitals overlap to the maximum extent. The d-orbitals involved in the hybridization may be either inner d-orbitals i.e. $(n-1)d$ or outer d-orbitals i.e. $nd$. The complexes formed are called inner orbitals complex (low spin complex) and outer orbital complex (high spin complex) respectively. Further the complexes can be paramagnetic or diamagnetic in nature. The drawbacks of this theory the that this involves number of assumptions and also does not explain the colour of the complex.

Answer the following questions :
(a) Predict whether $\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}$ is diamagnetic or paramagnetic and why? [Atomic number : Co = 27] [1]
(b) What is the coordination number of Co in $\mathrm{[Co(en)_2Cl_2]^+}$ ? [1]
(c) (i) Write the IUPAC name of the given complex : $\mathrm{[Pt(NH_3)_2Cl_2]^{2+}}$
(ii) Explain $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}$ is an inner orbital or outer orbital complex. [1 + 1]
OR
(c) Using valence bond theory, deduce the shape and hybridization of $\mathrm{[Ni(NH_3)_6]^{2+}}$
questions.solution:
(a) Paramagnetic, due presence of four unpaired electrons. [½ + ½]
(b) C.No. = 6 [1]
(c) (i) Diamminedichloridoplatinum (IV) [1]
(ii) It uses inner d-orbitals because $\mathrm{NH_3}$ causes pairing of electrons. [1]
OR
(c) $\mathrm{[Ni(NH_3)_6]^{2+}}$
Oxidation state of Ni = +2
Electronic configuration of Ni = $d^{8}$
If $\mathrm{NH_3}$ causes the pairing, then only one 3d orbital is empty. Thus, it cannot undergo $d^{2}sp^{3}$ hybridization. Therefore, it undergoes $sp^{3}d^{2}$ hybridization. [1]
Shape : Octahedral ; Hybridization = $sp^{3}d^{2}$ [½ + ½]

questions.stem:
In galvanic cell, chemical energy of a redox reaction is converted into electrical energy, whereas in an electrolytic cell the redox reaction occurs on passing electricity. The simplest galvanic cell is in which Zn rod is placed in a solution of $\mathrm{ZnSO_4}$ and Cu rod is placed in a solution of $\mathrm{CuSO_4}$. The two rods are connected by a metallic wire through a voltmeter. The two solutions are joined by a salt bridge. The difference between the two electrode potentials of the two electrodes is known as electromotive force. In the process of electrolysis, the decomposition of a substance takes place by passing an electric current. One mole of electric charge when passed through a cell will discharge half a mole of a divalent metal ion such as $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$. This was first formulated by Faraday in the form of laws of electrolysis

Answer the following questions :
(a) What is the function of a salt bridge in a galvanic cell ? [1]
(b) When does galvanic cell behave like an electrolytic cell ? [1]
(c) Can copper sulphate solution be stored in a pot made of zinc ? Explain with the help of the value of $E^\circ_{cell}$.
$E^\circ_{\mathrm{Cu^{2+}/Cu}} = 0.34\ \mathrm{V}$
$E^\circ_{\mathrm{Zn^{2+}/Zn}} = -0.76\ \mathrm{V}$ [2]
OR
(c) How much charge in terms of Faraday is required for the following :
(i) 1 mol of $\mathrm{MnO_4^{-}}$ to $\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}$
(ii) 1 mol of $\mathrm{H_2O}$ to $\mathrm{O_2}$ [2]
questions.solution:
(a) It connects the solution of two half cell to complete the circuit.
It maintains the electrical neutrality of the solution in order to give continuous flow or generation of current. [1]
(b) When $E_{ext} > 1.1\ \mathrm{V}$
(i) Electrons flow from Cu to Zn and current flows from Zn to Cu.
(ii) Zinc is deposited at the zinc electrode and copper dissolves at copper electrode [1]
(c) No, zinc is more reactive than copper
The reaction is, $\mathrm{Zn + CuSO_4 \rightarrow ZnSO_4 + Cu}$
Represent as $\mathrm{Zn \mid Zn^{2+} \parallel Cu^{2+} \mid Cu}$
$E^\circ_{cell} = 1.10\ \mathrm{V}$ [1]
As $E^\circ_{cell}$ is positive the reaction take place and we cannot store. [1]
OR
(c) (i) 5F [1]
(ii) 2F [1]

questions.stem:
Attempt any five of the following :
(a) Why Zinc is not regarded as a transition element ?
(b) What is Lanthanoid contraction ?
(c) Why is first ionization enthalpy of chromium lower than that of Zn ?
(d) Why are transition elements good catalysts ?
(e) Compounds of transition metals are generally coloured. Give reason.
(f) Out of $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ and $\mathrm{K_2MnO_4}$, which one is paramagnetic and why ?
(g) Complete the following ionic equation :
$\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-} + 14H^{+} + 6e^{-} \longrightarrow}$ [1 × 5]
questions.solution:
(a) Due to completely filled d-orbitals in their ground state as well as in oxidized state.
(b) The filling of 4f orbital before 5d orbital result in regular decrease in atomic radii or ionic radii called lanthanoid contraction / The regular decrease in the atomic or ionic radii of the elements with increase in atomic number.
(c) Because after removal of one $e^{-}$ Cr acquire half-filled stable configuration whereas Zn has completely filled 4s orbital so removal of one $e^{-}$ required more energy as compare to Cr.
(d) Due to variable oxidation state / unpaired electrons / Vacant d-orbital / provide large surface area.
(e) Due to d-d transition
(f) $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ is paramagnetic due to presence of unpaired electrons in Mn(VII) ion.
(g) $\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-} + 14H^{+} + 6e^{-} \longrightarrow 2Cr^{3+} + 7H_2O}$
(Any five) [1 × 5]

questions.stem:
(a) (i) Define reverse osmosis.
(ii) Why are aquatic species more comfortable in cold water in comparison to warm water?
(iii) A solution containing 2 g of glucose ($M = 180\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$) in 100 g of water is prepared at 303 K. If the vapour pressure of pure water at 303 K is 32.8 mm Hg, what would be the vapour pressure of the solution ? [1+1+3]
questions.solution:
(a) (i) If external pressure greater than osmotic pressure is applied, the flow of solvent molecules can be made to proceed from solution towards pure solvent, i.e., in reverse direction of the ordinary osmosis. [1]
(ii) Solubility of gases in water decreases with rise in temperature. More oxygen will be available in the cold water. [1]
(iii) $\frac{P_1^0 - P_S}{P_1^0} = \frac{n_{glucose}}{n_{H_2O}}$ [1]
$\frac{P_1^0 - P_S}{P_1^0} = \frac{w_g}{M_g} \times \frac{m_{(H_2O)}}{w_{(H_2O)}}$ [1]
$\frac{32.8 - P_S}{32.8} = \frac{2}{180} \times \frac{18}{100}$
$P_S = 32.73\ \mathrm{mm\ Hg}$ [1]
questions.or_stem:
(b) (i) Predict whether van't Hoff factor will be less or greater than one, when Ethanoic acid is dissolved in benzene.
(ii) Define ideal solution.
(iii) Calculate the mass of $\mathrm{CaCl_2}$ (molar mass = 111 g $\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$) to be dissolved in 500 g of water to lower its freezing point by 2K, assuming that $\mathrm{CaCl_2}$ undergoes complete dissociation.
($K_f$ for water = 1.86 K kg $\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$) [1 + 1 + 3]
questions.or_solution:
(b) (i) Van't Hoff factor will be less than one. [1]
(ii) Solution which obeys Raoult's law over the entire range of concentration called an Ideal solution. [1]
(iii) $\Delta T_f = iK_f m$
$\Delta T_f = iK_f \frac{w_2}{M_2} \times \frac{1000}{w_1}$
$\mathrm{CaCl_2 \rightarrow Ca^{2+} + 2Cl^{-}}$, $i = 3$ [1]
$w_2 = \frac{\Delta T_f \times M_2 \times w_1}{i \times K_f \times 1000}$
$w_2 = \frac{2 \times 111 \times 500}{3 \times 1.86 \times 1000}$ [1]
$= 19.89 \approx 20\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$ [1]
